steps.text: Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C).
Place unpeeled garlic cloves in the middle of a large square of aluminum foil. Drizzle cloves with 1 tablespoon olive oil; wrap in foil.
Roast in the preheated oven for 10 to 15 minutes until golden brown. Remove from the oven and allow to cool, 5 to 10 minutes.
Squeeze roasted garlic out of the peels into a food processor. Add garbanzo beans, tahini, lemon juice, cumin, salt, and remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil. Process until very creamy.

raw_recipe.headline: Authentic Kicked-Up Syrian Hummus
raw_recipe.description: One grandmother's Syrian hummus recipe is tweaked a bit with five cloves of sweet, nutty roasted garlic, making it a standout dip that everyone will love.
raw_recipe.name: Authentic Kicked-Up Syrian Hummus

review.reviewBody: WOW!!! I have had good hummus before but this recipe is without a doubt the best hummus I have ever tasted! Truly heavenly! The cumin and the roasted garlic really make the dish :)

I’ve made hummus maybe 5 times before, and I tried a couple of different recipes. The hummus I made with this recipe was not only the best I’ve ever made, it was the best I’ve ever eaten (and I lived in the Middle East for 2 years). I used only 2 cloves of garlic, roasted in a skillet on the stovetop. I added 1 tsp of Aleppo pepper and ⅛ tsp of ground cayenne pepper. And I cooked 1 cup of dried chickpeas in salted water for 3 hours and saved the aqua fava, which I used to get the right consistency when I was blending everything together. I recorded my changes and added this recipe to my permanent collection.

Roasting the garlic is a GAME CHANGER!! Soaked chick peas, then cooked in the pressure cooker also makes a difference. I used less tahini and lemon. All else them same. Finally, a hummus recipe to keep!

This is absolutely phenomenal! I did add a few things to kick it up and make it more to my preference. I like it a little creamier so I added a few extra drizzles of extra virgin olive oil. I also love olive tampenade, so I bought some whole kalamata olives from the Mediterranean olive bar at Wegmans. I put approximately 1/2 cup in the food processor with the hummus and then coarsely chopped another 1/2 cup for the tampenade. I can't believe how delicious it is. So much better than store bought, and EASY. I'll be making a lot more of this hummus and plan to try other tampenades soon.

This Hummus recipe is the best I've tried..
I don't have time to roast garlic so I just 
shred it into a pan with a little oil and 
brown it on the stove top.. gives the same 
affect.. also we like it with a little
smoked paprika and a little cayenne..

This was really good! I followed the original recipe (with the exception of using minced garlic from a jar instead of fresh) and thought it needed a little more flavor. So, I added extra cumin, some curry, another tablespoon of garlic, and 3/4 of a roasted red pepper. I also left most of the juice in the beans to avoid it being too thick. The consistency was perfect and the taste was great. It was very similar to the red pepper hummus at one of my favorite local places. I've tried to replicate it several times with no luck, so I am very pleased with this recipe! My main advice is to not lessen the amount of tahini. It's a strong flavor, but tahini makes hummus! Thanks for sharing. This is a keeper.

Delicious. A personal choice: Reduce salt, especially if serving with salted pita chips or bread. (We have a salt -sensitive family member.) We also reduced cumin to 1/2 teaspoon. Let it sit and add more seasoning if needed.

LOVED it! I added a pinch of cayenne red pepper in the mix and sprinkled with paprika to serve. I agree it’s a lot of lemon. I used 2 lemons to get 1/3 cup and next time might just use 1 large or 2 very small ones. Now, the tahini I bought was in the Kosher food area and when I got it home and looked at the ingredients it was basically hummus! ( tahini, chick peas and lemon). But was a nice creamy mixture so mine wasn’t too thick. Oh and I also put a few basil leaves in. Everyone loved it at the Super Bowl party. Served with carrots, celery and asparagus spears.

I added ground coriander, smoked paprika and finely grated parisian cheese. My husband says it was one of the best he's ever tasted (and I turned him on to middle eastern food 25 years ago. This is a very easy recipe to make, but it was a little thick, so I added back some of the water from my organic chick peas, then adjusted the amount of salt at the end. I will definitely make this again.

This, by far, is the best hummus recipe I have found! I did follow a review stating to use only 1 TB each of lemon juice and tahini per cup of garbanzo beans, though. The flavor is wonderful and creamy. I used some of the liquid from the beans instead of the remaining olive oil and omitted the salt. Upon tasting the base recipe, which as I stated, is the best I’ve had, I also blended in roasted red pepper and a roasted jalapeño pepper. Sometimes I can’t believe how easy hummus is to make!

Never made humus before, loved this recipe! I doubled the roasted garlic. First time I made it it was good but a little thick, but certainly wonderful to eat. Second time I made it I added an extra tablespoon of olive oil and a tablespoon of water and it made it a little bit creamier. It's enough for me. I will be keeping this recipe!
Because of disability, it can take days to complete a recipe. Fortunately I found red jalapenos at a Mexican grocery store, and a bag of peeled garlic from Aldi.
I added several tablespoons of the beans juice to make it more moist. Not enough liquid. I also added cayenne pepper to kick it up a notch. It was delicious!!

I've tried many hummus recipes and I think this is my favorite! I don't know if it was the recipe or the fact that I was able to get some tahini from Israel. I'm sure it would be ok with domestic source too. I forgot to add the olive oil to the garlic when I roasted it so I added it to the blender instead. Great recipe. I will look no further.
I loved this recipe This is the first time that I've made hummus and will definitely make this recipe again.

Easy to make with great flavor. I roasted a red bell pepper to mix in with the chick peas and to top the hummus with. Also added some chili pepper for heat. Def will make again. First time I attempted hummus, and so glad I did. Thanks for the base recipe.

It was great. Some hummus recipes call for un-roasted garlic and others call for garlic powder. It seems to me that roasted garlic results in the best flavor. I added some powdered cayenne once and ground red chile another. I preferred the cayenne. My biggest difficulty is keeping out of it until my wife comes home.
Followed the recipe and it was much better than the store.
My family loved it! I followed the recipe exactly. Easy to make, great flavor!
too salty for my taste. but good base recipe.
